newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks edge higher in buoyant trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks edge higher in buoyant trade.

text.p: Jordanian stocks edged up for the second day helped by improved investor sentiment on select demand and a healthy batch of first half results, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.24 percent to 146.31 points from 145.96 points on Sunday.
It was its highest level since March when it began a gradual slide that sent it in June to its lowest level for three years on a cash shortage and minimal institutional support.
A total of 525,953 shares changed hands on Monday in healthy 949,797 dinar turnover, dominated by a few bloc sales.
Dealers said that along with continuing select demand on key bluechip stock, early half-year results of leading banks and some industrial companies underpinned the market.

"Generally the results of the first six months of the year compared to the same period last year showed an improvement," Ummaya Toukan, the director general of the stock market, said in an interview on state television broadcast on Sunday night.
Improved sentiment kept up the same pattern of demand on key stock, including Arab Bank and Livestock and Poultry while bloc sales in Jordan Worsted Mills and Dar al-Dawa helped buttress volume.
Of 46 stocks traded, 21 advanced, 13 fell and 12 were unchanged. None posted year lows.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- rose 0.03 percent to 81.21 points. It was 14.98 percent down on last year.
In industrials, the leading sector, Livestock and Poultry again dominated activity with another 10 fils rise to 690 fils on a moderately high 166,041 dinar turnover.
Jordan Cement Factories, a focus of foreign investor interest, rose 10 fils to 3.350 dinars. Jordan Worsted Mills was unchanged at 7.100 dinars in a large bloc sale of 14,500 shares.

In banks, aside from market leader Arab Bank's, which was unchanged at 239.750 dinars, trade was minimal. Debt ridden Amman Investment Bank, currently in Central Bank sanctioned negotiations with the Arab Bank over a buyout, rose 10 fils to 240 fils. Islamic Bank rose 10 fils to 3.650 dinars.
In services, Jordan Electric Power rose 40 fils to 1.600 dinars with a low 29,723 dinar turnover. National Portfolio shed 10 fils to 1.200 dinars.

Industrials dominated on Monday, with a high 686,514 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.28 percent. Banks had a 184,033 turnover and a similar index rise of 0.28 percent while services had a lower 78,412 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.13 percent.

A total of 180,969 shares worth 102,098 dinars changed hands in moderate trade in the parallel market. Of 18 shares traded, four advanced, six declined and eight were unchanged. None posted a year low.
